description: The bar chart illustrates the “effect” of various multilingual BERT models—mBERT and XLM—on morphosyntactic features categorized by “case,” “gender,” “number,” and “tag,” with each model variant (L₂, R₂, B₂) represented by distinct colored bars and error bars indicating variability. The vertical axis, labeled “effect,” ranges from 0 to 20 with major ticks at intervals of 5, while the horizontal axis lists the four linguistic categories. For “case,” mBERT-L₂ (light blue) and XLM-L₂ (dark blue) show moderate effects around 6, mBERT-R₂ (light green) and XLM-R₂ (dark green) are lower (~2–3), and mBERT-B₂ (pink) and XLM-B₂ (red) are highest (~12–13). For “gender,” effects are generally lower: mBERT-L₂ (~1.5), XLM-L₂ (~0.5), mBERT-R₂ (~1.8), XLM-R₂ (~1), mBERT-B₂ (~4), and XLM-B₂ (~3). For “number,” all models show small effects: mBERT-L₂ (~1), XLM-L₂ (~0.8), mBERT-R₂ (~1), XLM-R₂ (~0.5), mBERT-B₂ (~2.5), and XLM-B₂ (~2). For “tag,” effects are minimal across all models, mostly near 0–1, with mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ slightly higher (~1). The legend on the right identifies each model variant by color. The bars are grouped by linguistic category, with error bars extending vertically to indicate uncertainty. No bars are sorted by height; instead, they are grouped by model type within each linguistic category. The chart visually emphasizes that B₂ variants generally outperform L₂ and R₂ variants, especially for “case,” while effects diminish for “gender,” “number,” and “tag.”
